name: TCS

Ninja.dsaDepth: Light — Foundation section only (numerical, verbal, reasoning); no coding interview typically required
rounds: TCS NQT: Foundation section (75 min, 65 questions, no negative marking)
extraTopics: Speed on straightforward quant and reasoning questions

Digital.dsaDepth: Moderate — Foundation plus Advanced (quant, reasoning, coding) sections
rounds: TCS NQT: Foundation + Advanced sections (115 more minutes: advanced quant, reasoning, coding)

Prime.dsaDepth: Moderate–Heavy — top NQT band, at least one fully solved Advanced coding problem, project-focused interview
rounds: TCS NQT: Foundation + Advanced, with a fully-solved Advanced coding problem expected
Extended technical interview including an AI/data project review
extraTopics: A deployable AI/data project you can explain end-to-end
Coding depth beyond the Digital track

ladder.title: Assistant System Engineer (Ninja track)
ladder.notes: Foundation-only NQT score; lowest of the three tracks

ladder.title: Assistant System Engineer (Digital track)
ladder.notes: Higher NQT score, Foundation + Advanced sections

ladder.title: Assistant System Engineer (Prime track)
ladder.notes: Top NQT scorers; extended interview, AI/data project expected

ladder.title: IT Analyst, System Engineer and above
ladder.notes: Lateral hiring uses role-specific rounds, not the NQT

roleFamilies: Assistant System Engineer (all tracks feed this title)
IT Analyst / System Engineer (experienced lateral hiring)

sources.title: TCS Recruitment 2026: Ninja, Digital, and Prime Track Guide (FACEPrep)
used: three tracks, CTC bands, NQT sections per track

sources.title: TCS NQT 2026: Ninja, Digital and Prime Tracks Explained (FACEPrep)
used: single unified NQT, track routing by score

rolesNotes: TCS restructured the old separate Ninja/Digital tests into one NQT with three tracks; the sources describe the 2026 process and are internally consistent. Lateral/lead-level rounds are not detailed here.
indiaNote: TCS hires almost entirely through the centralised NQT for freshers across India; the process described here is India-specific.
